profile.address: Lookout Drive, Garland, Dallas County, Texas, 75082
profile.reading: This point is mapped to Lookout Drive in Garland, TX, without a house number, placing it somewhere on NTT's real Dallas-area data center campus. NTT's own site confirms two buildings by street address on Lookout Drive: TX1 at 2008 Lookout Dr (230,000 square feet, 16 megawatts of critical IT load, with SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 High, and HIPAA compliance attestations) and TX4 at 2060 Lookout Dr (127,000 square feet, 36 megawatts, part of a 124-megawatt campus, stated as becoming available from June 2026). Data center directory Baxtel additionally lists TX2 at 2108 Lookout Dr and TX3 at 2080 Lookout Dr, both roughly 229,500 square feet and operational since 2024, though MW figures for TX2 and TX3 are not disclosed in that secondary source. Because this specific mapped point lacks a house number, this entry cannot confirm which of NTT's four Lookout Drive buildings it corresponds to, and does not guess; it is presented here as part of the shared Garland, TX data center campus rather than assigned false building-specific figures. RagingWire (NTT's US brand) announced the campus in 2022 as a planned 1-million-square-foot, 80-megawatt-plus development, since expanded further per the individual building figures above. Data Center Frontier toured TX1 and reports the Garland campus was established in 2016 on the former RagingWire site and has been operational since 2017, with the 42-acre megacampus ultimately planned to hold over one million square feet and 144 megawatts of critical IT load at full buildout. NTT announced a 50 million dollar fit out of the TX2 and TX3 buildings in June 2023, adding nearly 300,000 square feet of data vault and office space with each building rated at 36 megawatts, using air cooled chillers with fan coil wall designs distinct from TX1s original cooling configuration. A further 42 million dollar, 236,000 square foot fourth building was reported under construction from September 2025 through an expected April 2026 completion, expanding the 47 acre site. Cushman and Wakefield market data cited alongside that expansion put existing Dallas-Fort Worth data center capacity at 4.5 million square feet by the end of 2023 with only 178,000 square feet available for lease, reflecting the tight vacancy driving continued campus growth at this site.

reading.body:
NTT's Dallas campus on Lookout Drive in Garland consists of four buildings, of which TX1 and TX4 are published with 16 megawatts and 36 megawatts of critical IT load respectively. NTT states the full campus will reach 124 megawatts at buildout. The campus opened in 2017 on a 42-acre site and has expanded continuously, with TX2 and TX3 (each 36 megawatts according to secondary sources, though NTT has not published these figures) completed in 2024 after a 50 million dollar investment, and a fourth building under construction as of September 2025 for completion in April 2026. TX1 holds SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 High, and HIPAA attestations, qualifying it for regulated workloads including healthcare and finance.

At full buildout, 124 megawatts of IT load at typical AI training density, assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, translates to roughly 3,100 racks. The campus ranks 19th among Texas facilities with published capacity, though only 18 of 133 mapped facilities in the state disclose megawatt figures, making this ranking's denominator small. Published capacity in Texas totals 468 megawatts, of which this campus represents 26 percent. The Dallas-Fort Worth market as of late 2023 had 4.5 million square feet of data center space with only 178,000 square feet available for lease, indicating the tight supply that has driven NTT's continued expansion here.

The campus expanded again from September 2025 with a planned 236,000 square foot fourth building, suggesting NTT views Dallas power availability and business demand as sufficient to justify continued investment beyond the originally announced 144 megawatts of ultimate campus capacity. Whether this buildout is complete or will proceed as announced is not published.
